nodes.label: Preload only on routes where the hero image is really the LCP element
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - t9-lcp-preload-contract [ses_f1696bb14ffeRoKS2rSP804CT3].md:L29] Preloading an image that is not the largest contentful paint makes the real LCP slower, because the browser spends bandwidth on the wrong resource; the audit found most pages have no above-the-fold image, or only 24 to 64 pixel chrome, where a preload would be actively harmful. The brief was rescoped on exactly this ground: the count "239 of 242 rows lack a preload" was true and the inference drawn from it was wrong.
nodes.norm_label: preload only where the hero image is really the lcp

nodes.label: Guard the invariant with a structural test derived from source, not a hand list
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - t9-lcp-preload-contract [ses_f1696bb14ffeRoKS2rSP804CT3].md:L58] Guard the property structurally, not as a hand list, because a hand list is the mechanism that let this drift: the rule is derived by scanning the rendered source across src/pages/** so a new route that promotes an image is caught without anyone editing a list.
nodes.norm_label: structural invariant test not a hand list

nodes.label: A preload scan over page files must walk component imports, or hero-owning pages look clean
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - t9-lcp-preload-contract [ses_f1696bb14ffeRoKS2rSP804CT3].md:L8175] A first RED run exposed a flaw in the test rather than the code: the scan only looked at inline in page files, so index.astro and blog/index.astro looked clean because their heroes live in Hero.astro / BlogHero.astro. The scan was widened to walk component imports (BFS, stopping at src/layouts/**), after which the rule named exactly the four audit targets.
nodes.norm_label: lcp preload scan must walk component imports

nodes.label: fetchpriority is the positive authorial LCP claim; loading="eager" is not
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - t9-lcp-preload-contract [ses_f1696bb14ffeRoKS2rSP804CT3].md:L8237] Eager alone is not an LCP claim: lp/campaign.astro has loading="eager" on a 28x28 topbar logo and its LCP is the h1, so a preload there is the exact harm the rescoping was meant to prevent. The guard was keyed on fetchpriority instead, with the exclusion pinned by a dedicated test. The note records the remaining gap: a future hero that gets loading="eager" but forgets fetchpriority will not be caught.
nodes.norm_label: fetchpriority is the positive lcp claim

nodes.label: Blog cover dimensions are absent from the D1 schema, so imagesizes must come from CSS
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - t9-lcp-preload-contract [ses_f1696bb14ffeRoKS2rSP804CT3].md:L8198] blog_posts has no cover_image_width / cover_image_height columns; BlogPost carries only cover_image_url and cover_image_alt, so there is no intrinsic size to read. The handling recorded here is to derive imagesizes from the stylesheet slot (740px container minus 48px padding, capped at 480px by object-fit) and guard the whole payload on the nullable URL, so a post without a cover emits no link rather than undefined into markup.
nodes.norm_label: blog cover dimensions absent from d1 schema

nodes.label: LCP preload cache-key duplication
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - t9-lcp-preload-contract [ses_f1696bb14ffeRoKS2rSP804CT3].md:L3451] The live-demo poster renders ${SITE_POSTER_URL}?v=20260926, so the preload must carry the same ?v= query string or it is a different cache key and the poster downloads twice. The duplicated literal was extracted into a POSTER_URL const to stop the three copies drifting apart.

nodes.label: No maintained pure-Rust YouTube extractor exists; the ecosystem moved to yt-dlp plus a JS runtime
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7703] Documented, not inferred. rustube last published 2022-10-16 with 24 open issues and no maintainer replies; the best-maintained pure-Rust extractor, rusty_ytdl, admits in its own issues #52/#53 that its crates.io release is out of date and 403s, with its android_vr and PO-token fixes never shipped. The yt-dlp crate's own README states it moved off rustube "due to frequent breaking changes on the YouTube website". The one crate that works, ytdown, is a 3.5-month-old, 3-star, 214-download repo: a research spike, not a dependency.

nodes.label: yt-dlp player_client selection and PO Token policy
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7709] Per the PO-Token Guide, without a PO token "requests for the affected clients' format URLs may return HTTP Error 403, or result in your account or IP address being blocked", and the token is now bound to the video ID. The enforcement table is the decision-relevant artefact: tv, android_vr and web_embedded need no PO token, web is SABR-only, and the android/ios clients 403 on ranges past roughly 256 KiB. The recorded workaround is to force --extractor-args "youtube:player_client=android_vr,tv,web_embedded" rather than proxy.
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp player client and po token policy

nodes.label: googlevideo HTTP header requirements: the IFrame player needs a Referer, the CDN does not
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7787] yt-dlp never sends a Referer on the media download and still works: grepping the current YouTube extractor yields exactly one Referer, at _base.py:1015 inside _download_ytcfg, and only for the web_embedded client fetching the client-config webpage. Error 153 is scoped by YouTube's own IFrame Player API reference to the embedder identity, not to the CDN, so the premise behind the current rejection does not apply to a direct media URL.

nodes.label: googlevideo URL expiry, IP binding and signature
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7796] The real authorisation is in the signed URL and it is IP-bound, not header-bound. The sparams signed set is expire,ei,ip,id,itag,source,requiressl,xpc,gcr,siu,bui,spc,vprv,svpuc,mime,ns,rqh,gir,clen,dur,lmt with no referer, while the client IP is embedded in both query form (ip=83.34.78.41) and path form (/ip/59.11.11.11/), so reusing a URL from another network 403s.
nodes.norm_label: googlevideo url expiry ip binding and signature

nodes.label: Extend the existing custom protocol for Range, not a local HTTP server
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7771] tauri-plugin-localhost v2.3.2 is the wrong tool: it uses tiny_http with no range handling at all, serves app assets rather than being a media proxy, and its own docs state "This plugin brings considerable security risks" because the server has no authentication. Range is also not free with a custom protocol, since Tauri's built-in handler has zero occurrences of range/206/Content-Range, but register_asynchronous_uri_scheme_protocol hands you the full http::Request so 206 is feasible, and the asset protocol is the in-tree precedent that implements it with http_range. A hand-rolled 127.0.0.1 server additionally has no CSP port wildcard, so the port must be pinned.
nodes.norm_label: custom protocol beats local http server for range

nodes.label: yt-dlp PyInstaller GPLv3+ licensing trap for vendoring
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7826] Verbatim from the project: "Most notably, the PyInstaller-bundled executables include GPLv3+ licensed code, and as such the combined work is licensed under GPLv3+", while the git repo, PyPI sdist and wheel are Unlicense-only. On Linux that leaves exactly two shippable artefacts and both are bad: yt-dlp_linux (39 MB, the recommended standalone) is a GPLv3+ combined work, and the zipimport yt-dlp needs Python 3.10+ on the user's machine.

nodes.label: yt-dlp release verification is GPG-only, so the app's minisign updater verification is not reusable
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7812] Verified against the live release 2026.08.19: the only verification artefacts are SHA2-256SUMS(+sig) and SHA2-512SUMS(+sig), and there is no .minisig. A Rust app that later vendors the binary must ship and pin public.key and implement OpenPGP verification (for example the pgp crate) or shell out to gpg; the existing minisign-based Tauri updater verification does not transfer. yt-dlp publishes no official statement either endorsing or forbidding third-party redistribution, verified by heading enumeration of the master README, so that decision is left to the app's own licence analysis.
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp verification is gpg only not minisign

nodes.label: yt-dlp resolve-and-stream audio path as the minimum viable first increment
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7844] Increment 1 is resolve-and-stream with no proxy and no bundled binary. The justification chains the other findings: the pure-Rust alternative is not maintained, the Referer premise behind the current rejection is wrong for direct media URLs so option (a) is viable, (a) needs no CSP entry because media-src already allows https://*.googlevideo.com and needs no listener, no disk and no new tokio feature, and the GPLv3 finding forbids bundling the binary yet. Bundling, the yt-dlp Rust wrapper crate, the Range byte proxy, a PO-token provider, a JS runtime, HLS and auth are each deferred with their reason.
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp resolve and stream audio path

nodes.label: --ignore-config is mandatory when an app shells out to yt-dlp
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7854] Otherwise a user's yt-dlp.conf can inject --cookies-from-browser, --remote-components or proxy settings into the app's subprocess. The flag's existence is verified; the reasoning is recorded as inference rather than documented fact.
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp ignore-config is mandatory in a sandboxed app

nodes.label: WebKitGTK disables HLS by default and gates MP4/AAC on installed GStreamer plugins
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7803] WebKitGTK 2.38.4 disabled HLS media playback by default, so the web_safari HLS escape hatch is unavailable to a Tauri v2 Linux webview without WEBKIT_GST_ENABLE_HLS_SUPPORT=1, and even then native HLS in <audio> is unsupported because WebKit has no HLS audio path. Separately, WebKit bug #135972 documents that MP4/AAC support is gated on installed GStreamer plugins such as gst-plugins-libav, which is why audio/webm opus (itag 251) is preferred over audio/mp4 (itag 140) and the resolve should be gated on canPlayType at runtime.
nodes.norm_label: webkitgtk hls disabled and codecs gated by gstreamer
